4582.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *árktos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos (“bear”). Cognates include Latin ursus, Welsh arth, Sanskrit ऋक्ष (ṛ́kṣa), Old Armenian արջ (arǰ), and Albanian ari.

4576.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂élbʰit. Cognates include Albanian elb.

4501.t: Etymology tree Proto-Indo-European *né Proto-Indo-European *n̥- Proto-Hellenic *ə- Ancient Greek ἀ- (a-)? Proto-Indo-European *demh₂-der.

4579.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + πεῖρα (peîra, “trial, attempt”) + -ος (-os). Compare with Latin peritus.

4502.t: From ἀ- (ă-, “un-”) + θάνατος (thắnătos, “dying”). Sense 4, referring to certain soldiers in Achaemenid Persia, has an uncertain origin.

4578.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aksōn, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs-. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀰𐀚 (a-ko-so-ne), Sanskrit अक्ष (akṣa, “axle, axis, balance beam”) and Latin axis.

4572.t: From ἅλς (háls, “salt, sea”) + -εύς (-eús, suffix for person concerned).

4508.t: Disputed. Commonly held to be formed from ἄκρος (ákros, “sharp”) and another element of uncertain provenance, e.g. εἴβω (eíbō, “to drop, let fall”) according to Schwyzer, though this is rejected by Beekes & van Beek.

4583.t: According to Beekes, of Pre-Greek origin due to the similarity with ἄχυρον (ákhuron, “chaff”) and the vocalic interchange υ/ω.

4535.t: From ἀν- (an-, “not”) + ὄφελος (óphelos, “advantage, help”) + -ης (-ēs, adjective suffix).

4581.t: From ἀ- (a-, not) + πίμπλημι (pímplēmi, “to fill full, satisfy, satiate”) + -τος (-tos).

4587.t: Uncertain. Beekes hesitantly suggest a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *g⁽ʷ⁾ow- (“hand”).

4557.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “away, from, off”) + τρέπω (trépō, “turn”) from Proto-Indo-European *trep-.

4550.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “to, toward”) + σβέννυμι (sbénnūmi, “to quench, to be quenched”).

4543.t: From ἀπαλλάσσω (apallássō, “to release, deliver”) + -σείω (-seíō, desiderative suffix)

4514.t: Ritual term of unknown origin. Fur.: 298 compares λιγνύς (lignús, “smoke, soot”), which supposes a prothetic vowel and interchange σ/zero before velar (highly uncertain).
